items.text: Only 6 of the 8 listed teams exist on disk. scenario-debug and scenario-refactor are missing from scenarios/prompt-manager/store/teams/. The 6 present teams are: director-swarm (enabled), marketing-crew, revenue-research, meta-optimization, scenario-feature, and scenario-qa (enabled).

The prompt builder (prompt_builder.go) currently reads only SpawnMode, DecisionMode, and DisplayName from the Team struct. All rich context — mission details, operating procedures, workflows — comes from TEAM.md as freeform markdown. This means v2 fields need prompt builder updates to be rendered as natural language in heartbeat prompts.

CurrentSchemaVersion in common.go is a global constant (=1) shared across ALL entity types (skills, agents, teams, etc.). Bumping it to 2 for teams would affect all entities. Per-entity versioning may be needed, or the existing schemaVersion field in each JSON file (which is already per-file) could be relied on instead of the Go constant.

Draft v2 field values have been produced for all 6 existing teams based on TEAM.md, HEARTBEAT.md, and RESPONSIBILITIES.md analysis. See conclusion.md Finding 4 for the complete per-team breakdown of objectives, KPIs, consumers, and contributions.

TEAM.md content analysis shows a clear split: objectives/goals, consumer relationships, and contribution types can move to structured fields. Operating procedures, workflows, methodologies, brand voice, quality rubrics, charter boundaries, and skill references are inherently freeform and must stay in TEAM.md.

items.context: The spec lists 8 teams to audit, but only 6 exist on disk. scenario-debug and scenario-refactor have no team.json, TEAM.md, or any other files. We can't draft v2 values for teams that don't exist yet.

options.label: Proceed with 6 teams only; draft values for missing teams when they are created
options.rationale: The 2 missing teams are disabled anyway. Creating stub files just for schema design adds no value — the real content will be written when the teams are actually designed.

options.label: Create minimal stubs for scenario-debug and scenario-refactor now with placeholder v2 values
options.rationale: Ensures the migration covers all 8 teams at once. But placeholder values have no grounding in real team design.

items.topic: Schema versioning strategy for the Team entity
items.context: CurrentSchemaVersion in common.go is a global constant (=1) used by ALL entity types. Bumping it to 2 just for teams would imply all entities are v2. However, each JSON file already has its own schemaVersion field that's independent of the Go constant.

options.label: Use per-file schemaVersion only; leave the Go constant at 1
options.rationale: Each team.json already has schemaVersion: 1. Bump it to 2 in the JSON files only. The Go code reads the file's version and handles both. No impact on other entity types.

options.label: Introduce a per-entity-type version constant (TeamSchemaVersion = 2)
options.rationale: More explicit in Go code. Allows different entity types to evolve independently with compile-time constants. But adds complexity.

options.label: Bump the global CurrentSchemaVersion to 2 and migrate all entities simultaneously
options.rationale: Simplest conceptually but forces all entities to be treated as v2 even if only teams changed.

items.context: The orchestration summary decided dependencies should be computed, not stored. The question is how to expose this computation. Options range from a CLI command to an API endpoint to both.

options.label: prompt-manager CLI command only (e.g., `prompt-manager graph team-dependencies`)
options.rationale: Fits the existing prompt-manager graph command family. Agents and humans can invoke it. No new API surface needed.

options.label: Both CLI command and API endpoint on the teams overview
options.rationale: The teams overview endpoint (mentioned in orchestration summary) could include computed dependencies in its response. CLI wraps the API.

options.label: Defer dependencies computation to a separate research item
options.rationale: The core v2 schema (objectives, kpis, consumers, contributions) is the priority. Dependencies computation is a separate concern that can be designed independently.

plan_updates: Created initial conclusion.md with: research question, summary, methodology, 7 findings (missing teams, Go model analysis, prompt builder usage, draft v2 values for all 6 teams, TEAM.md content split, dependencies computation approach, migration path), limitations, and 3 follow-up actions (implement v2 struct, trim TEAM.md, computed dependencies command).
